examples.goal: See as much of the car as possible while judging a finish.

settings.Shift+E: press to hide the popout panel

examples.result: The canvas has the full width. Press Shift+E again to bring the panel back.

examples.title: Start one zone over
examples.goal: Throw away experiments on one zone only.

settings.Reset Zone: press at the top of the panel

examples.result: Finish, colours, patterns and sliders of that zone go back to defaults. Other zones are untouched.

combos.why: The cards do quick actions like mute and duplicate; the panel does the detailed editing.
COLOR and APPLY AREA inside the panel are where every pixel rule lives.
The Hue Shift, Saturation and Brightness sliders in BASE are explained there.

faq.q: Where did my sliders go?
faq.a: They appear only after a Base Material or finish is chosen for the zone. Pick one in BASE.

faq.q: How do I hide the panel?
faq.a: Click the zone editor tab on the left of the canvas, or press Shift+E while the panel is open.

faq.q: Does hiding the panel change the zone?
faq.a: No. It only hides or shows the panel.

faq.q: What does Reset Zone reset?
faq.a: Only the open zone: its finish, colours, patterns and sliders. Reset All Zones in the left column resets every zone.

faq.q: Why is there no RESTRICT TO LAYERS box?
faq.a: It only shows when a layered template such as a PSD is loaded.

mistakes.symptom: Pressing E does not open the panel
mistakes.cause: A bare E is the eraser tool. The shortcut is Shift+E.
mistakes.fix: Use Shift+E, or click the zone editor tab on the left of the canvas.

mistakes.symptom: The panel is open but you cannot find Brightness
mistakes.cause: The zone has no Base Material yet, so the BASE sliders are not built.
mistakes.fix: Press Base Material and choose a finish.

mistakes.symptom: Shift+E does nothing
mistakes.cause: The panel has never been opened, because the shortcut only works while the panel is open.
mistakes.fix: Click a zone card first, then press Shift+E.

protips: Fold sections you are finished with by clicking their header. A long panel gets short again.
A messy zone does not need Reset All Zones: open that zone and press Reset Zone at the top of its panel. Every other zone keeps its settings.

articles.title: Zone presets and templates
articles.summary: Presets give you a ready-made zone layout, and templates save your own layout so you can reuse it on another paint.
articles.what: Presets Gallery (Zones > More) shows ready-made layouts; click one to load it. Each swatch shows the zone finishes. Save as Template stores your current zone layout under a name you choose, up to 60 characters; Load Template brings it back on another paint, and Shift+T opens the template library.
when: You want a quick starting look.
You have a layout you will use on several cars.
You want the same zone layout on several cars of a team.
how: 1. Open More above the zone list and press Presets Gallery. Click a preset.
2. To save your own, press Save as Template, type a name and press Save.
3. To reuse it, pick it from the Load Template dropdown on the new paint.

controls.label: Presets Gallery
controls.effect: Browse ready-made zone layouts / looks and apply one.

controls.label: Save as Template
controls.effect: Saves the current zone layout as a named template.

controls.label: Load Template... dropdown
controls.effect: Dropdown of your saved zone templates; choosing one loads it.

controls.label: e.g. My 3-Color Layout (max 60 chars)
controls.effect: use a descriptive name you'll recognize later

tips: Use a descriptive template name, such as "3-colour layout".
pitfalls: A template stores zone layouts, not your paint.

deep.heading: Three different libraries
deep.body: Presets Gallery holds 23 ready-made zone layouts in five groups: Show Car (4), Clean (2), Aggressive (6), Special Effect (6) and Themed (5). The Shokker Library, also opened with Shift+T, holds 12 livery templates such as Racing Stripe, Two-Tone Split, GT3 Livery and NASCAR Cup. Save as Template and the Load Template dropdown are your own saved layouts, kept on this computer.

deep.heading: Presets replace your zones at once
deep.body: Clicking a preset card swaps in its zones straight away, with no confirm box, and the toast reads Loaded preset. A preset leaves most colours empty on purpose: you click your own colours with the eyedropper afterwards. Only the quick colours are set, such as White for sponsors, Dark for dark areas and Remaining for the safety net. Save your own layout first if you want it back.

deep.heading: Livery templates ask before replacing
deep.body: Applying a livery template asks to confirm when your zones already hold a finish or colour, saying your current zones will be replaced. It can be undone with Ctrl+Z. The library header reminds you to paint region masks with the brush after loading, because templates bring finishes, not areas.

deep.heading: What your own template remembers
deep.body: A saved template keeps each zone's name, colour choices and tolerances, base, pattern, special finish, intensity, scale, locks and pattern stack. It does not keep drawn boxes, lassos, brush areas or layer limits. Names run up to 60 characters, and saving under the same name overwrites the old one. Loading a template can be undone.

deep.heading: A template is a layout, not a paint
deep.body: Because colour picks are stored, a template made on one car often fits another car with the same colours, but a different livery needs new picks. When none of the loaded zones has a finish, the toast adds that you should now assign finishes.

examples.title: Start from a preset and make it yours
examples.goal: Use Multi-Color Show Car as a skeleton.

settings.Result: 8 zones: Body Color 1 to 4, Car Number, Sponsors / Logos, Dark Areas, Everything Else
settings.Next: pick each body colour with PICK COLOR FROM CAR; delete unused zones

examples.result: A full set of finishes is ready and only your colours are missing.

examples.title: Save a reusable layout
examples.goal: Keep a 3-colour setup for the next car.
examples.result: The name appears in the Load Template dropdown. Draw any boxes again after loading.

examples.title: Try a livery template safely
examples.goal: Preview NASCAR Cup zones without losing your work.
examples.result: Your zones are replaced by the template's four zones. Press Ctrl+Z to return.

combos.why: The recipe shows how to build by hand the same plan that presets and templates give you in one click.
Presets Gallery, Save as Template, Shokker Library and Undo History all sit in the More menu.
A template is only zones. Save SHOKK also keeps your paint and finishes in one file.

faq.q: Can I undo a preset?
faq.a: A preset swaps in immediately and shows no confirm box. Save your zones as a template first if you may want them back.

faq.q: Where are my templates stored?
faq.a: On this computer, inside the app. They are not in your paint file and do not travel to another PC.

faq.q: Why did a loaded template cover the whole car?
faq.a: Templates do not store drawn areas. The zone kept its colour rule only. Draw its area again.

faq.q: What is the difference between a preset and a template?
faq.a: Presets are built-in layouts. Templates are either the 12 livery templates in the Shokker Library or your own saved ones.

faq.q: Is there a limit on the template name?
faq.a: 60 characters. Use a name you will recognise, like 3-colour layout.

mistakes.symptom: You clicked a preset and lost your zones
mistakes.cause: Presets replace the whole zone list immediately.
mistakes.fix: Save as Template before you open the Presets Gallery, so your list can be loaded back from the Load Template dropdown.

mistakes.symptom: A preset shows no colour change on the car
mistakes.cause: Most preset zones start without a colour pick and cover nothing yet.
mistakes.fix: Select each zone and use PICK COLOR FROM CAR on the matching colour.

mistakes.symptom: Saved template did not remember a layer limit
mistakes.cause: Templates store finishes and colours, not layer restrictions or drawn areas.
mistakes.fix: Use MAKE ZONE on the layer cards again after loading.

protips: Name templates by job, such as 2-colour with chrome numbers, not by car. The layout is what carries over.
The Shokker Library header tells you to paint region masks after loading. Treat library templates as a finish plan, not a finished livery.

articles.title: Why my zone does not show
articles.summary: A zone that does nothing almost always has one of a few simple causes: no finish, no way to pick pixels, a zone above it, a mute, or a layer that is missing.
articles.what: Shokker tells you on the zone card. The messages are: "Zone is muted. Click the eye icon to unmute", "Empty zone: pick a base finish AND a color (or draw a region)", "No finish assigned: pick a base material", "No color or region defined: this zone will not affect any pixels", and a warning when the zone is restricted to a layer that no longer exists. If the card says "ready to render" and you still see nothing, a zone higher in the list is probably claiming the same pixels. Check the colour tolerance too: if it is too tight the zone catches almost nothing.
when: You set a finish and the car looks the same.
A zone works in the overlay but not in the preview.
how: 1. Read the message on the zone card.
2. Click the eye icon to make sure the zone is not muted.
3. Give it a finish in BASE if none is set, and a colour, layer or box if none is set.
4. Drag the zone above others that overlap, or mute the others to test.
5. Raise the colour tolerance if the area is caught only in part.

controls.label: Zone eye / duplicate / link / x icons on each zone card
controls.effect: Eye hides a zone for testing, the copy icon duplicates, the x deletes it.

controls.label: Colour tolerance (sliders next to the colour chips)
controls.effect: How close a pixel must be to the picked colour to belong to the zone (about 30-50 normal; 6 = exact shade, 100 = loose).

controls.label: Base Material (finish picker button)
controls.effect: Opens the finish picker popup: bases (gloss, matte, satin, chrome, candy, pearl, metallic ...) and special looks. Shows the current finish name.

tips: Foundation finishes change only the shine when the colour is "Use source paint". They do not repaint, so the car can look the same colour.
pitfalls: Base Strength 0 makes a zone add nothing even when it is set up correctly.

deep.heading: The card checks these in a fixed order
deep.body: The card tests, in this order: muted, then tied to a missing layer, then completely empty, then no finish, then no colour or area, and finally ready. Only the first problem is shown. The small dot beside the name follows the same order: green is Will render, red is a missing layer, orange is a missing finish or missing pixels, grey is muted or empty. Fix the first message, look again, and a second one may appear.

deep.heading: Ready to render does not prove it shows
deep.body: The check only looks at what the zone has set. It cannot see that a zone above already owns the same pixels, that a Color Match is too tight, or that the layer you tied it to is under 50 percent opaque. All of those leave the card green. The fastest test is to mute zones above yours one at a time and watch LIVE PREVIEW.

deep.heading: Settings that make a good zone look like nothing
deep.body: A Foundation finish with Base Color set to Use source paint (spec only) changes only the shine, so colours stay identical. A Base Strength or Spec Strength of 0 removes the effect. A zone whose finish matches what is already there, such as gloss over gloss, changes nothing visible. To prove a zone catches the right pixels, set it to Chrome for a moment, then switch it back.

deep.heading: When the preview is the problem
deep.body: If the preview cannot finish it keeps showing the last good picture, and your newest change appears to do nothing. The red bar says so. Press F5 to rebuild. The usual cause of repeated failure is too many zones that have their own painted area, about 20 or more. A render with no valid zone is refused with a message asking for a zone with a colour and a finish, and muted zones are skipped.

deep.heading: Layer zones fail on purpose
deep.body: A zone tied to a hidden or missing layer paints nothing, deliberately, so it cannot spill onto other art. A hidden layer gives a one-time message. A deleted layer gives the red dot. A layer set below 50 percent opacity never owns its pixels.

faq.q: The card says Zone is ready to render, but I see nothing. Why?
faq.a: Something outside the zone is in the way: a zone above, a tight Color Match, a layer under 50 percent opacity, or a shine-only setting.

faq.q: What does the orange dot mean?
faq.a: Either the zone has no finish or it has no colour, layer or area. The card message says which.

faq.q: Why does a Foundation zone not change my colour?
faq.a: With Use source paint (spec only) it changes only the shine map. That is its job.

faq.q: My preview does not update.
faq.a: The preview may have failed and is showing the last good picture. Press F5, or click the red bar.

faq.q: Is a muted zone deleted?
faq.a: No. Click its eye icon to turn it back on.

mistakes.symptom: You picked a colour and finish but the zone card is still orange
mistakes.cause: One of the two is missing: the card checks both.
mistakes.fix: Read the card text. It names the missing half, either a finish or a colour, layer or area.

mistakes.symptom: RENDER refuses with a message about no zones
mistakes.cause: No active zone has both a colour and a finish. Muted zones are skipped.
mistakes.fix: Pick a colour on the paint for at least one zone, give it a Base Material, and unmute it if its eye is crossed out.

mistakes.symptom: Zone vanished after you tied it to a layer
mistakes.cause: The layer is hidden or below 50 percent opacity, so the zone owns no pixels.
mistakes.fix: Show the layer, raise its opacity to at least 50 percent, or clear the restriction.

protips: Set a suspect zone to Chrome with Use finish's own color for ten seconds. If nothing turns mirror-bright, the problem is its pixel rules, not its finish.
A render with no valid zone is refused with a clear message. Muted zones are skipped, so an all-muted list also counts as no zones.

articles.title: Recipe: split a car into body, hood, roof and trim
articles.summary: A clean starting plan: one zone for the body colour, one each for hood, roof and trim, and Everything Else at the bottom as the safety net.
articles.what: This is the same plan a typical livery needs. Shokker starts you with four open zones plus Everything Else, so you only need to fill them in. Aim the specific zones first (trim and numbers by layer, hood and roof by box or part), and let the body colour zone and Everything Else take the rest.
when: You have a finished livery and want different finishes on its main parts.
how: 1. Load your paint. Use a layered template if you can.
2. Zone 1, trim or stripes: PICK COLOR FROM CAR on the stripe colour; BASE > a finish such as satin.
3. Zone 2, hood: under APPLY AREA press Draw box over the hood; give it a finish.
4. Zone 3, roof: Draw box over the roof; finish.
5. Zone 4, body: PICK COLOR FROM CAR on the body colour; finish.
6. Leave Everything Else at the bottom for the rest, then check the preview and RENDER.

deep.heading: Why this order works
deep.body: Each zone gets first pick of the pixels it matches, then the next zone, and Everything Else takes what is left. So the narrowest rules go first: trim by colour or layer, then hood and roof by box, then the body colour, then Everything Else. Hood and roof must sit above the body zone. If the body zone were higher it would claim the red on the hood before the hood zone could.

deep.heading: Box plus colour, or box alone
deep.body: A hood zone with a colour and a box catches only that colour inside the box, which keeps hood graphics and decals out of the finish. A hood zone with only a box covers everything on that island, graphics included. Pick colour plus box when the hood carries artwork you want left alone.

deep.heading: A shine ladder for the four zones
deep.body: The base finishes form a ladder from dull to bright: Matte is metal 0, roughness 200, clearcoat 160. Satin is 0, 95, 70. Gloss is 0, 30, 16. Metallic is 200, 50, 16. Candy is 200, 15, 16. In the spec map the middle number is roughness, so a lower number means a smoother, brighter reflection, and clearcoat 16 is the maximum gloss. Use two or three steps apart, not neighbours, so zones read as different on the car.

deep.heading: Reach by role
deep.body: Numbers by layer need no colour. If you pick the fill, 10 to 16 keeps the outline out. Stripes and trim work at 25 to 35 because they are flat colours. Large body colours at 40 handle shading. Looser than 50 starts to grab neighbours.

deep.heading: Checking the result
deep.body: After each zone, glance at LIVE PREVIEW before adding the next. If a zone shows nothing, click its eye on the zones above yours. When you are happy, press RENDER once. Fewer than six zones keeps the preview quick.

faq.q: How many zones does a typical car need?
faq.a: Two or three. The recipe's four plus Everything Else is a full plan.

faq.q: Why not one zone per colour?
faq.a: You can, but shared looks should share a zone, because every extra zone adds work to the render.

faq.q: Should the hood box include the whole island?
faq.a: Yes, or slightly more. The hood and roof are different rectangles on the flat sheet, so draw each separately.

faq.q: Can I do this by talking instead?
faq.a: Yes. Chat understands matte black hood, carbon roof and builds the same zones for you.

faq.q: What if the body colour is also on the roof?
faq.a: That is the case the box handles: the roof zone is above the body zone and takes its island first.

mistakes.symptom: The hood shows the body finish instead of its own
mistakes.cause: The body zone sits above the hood zone and claimed the hood's colour first.
mistakes.fix: Drag the hood zone above the body zone.

mistakes.symptom: Hood and roof both changed from one zone
mistakes.cause: One box spanned both islands on the flat sheet.
mistakes.fix: Draw a separate box for each, in separate zones.

mistakes.symptom: Numbers lost their finish
mistakes.cause: The numbers zone sits below the body zone.
mistakes.fix: Move the numbers zone to the top of the list.

protips: Separate finishes by at least two steps on the matte, satin, gloss ladder. Neighbouring steps look the same from a distance.
Build with MAKE ZONE from layer cards when you have a layered template. It skips colour picking and cannot bleed.
